newsitem.title: UK: Intertanko concerned at Venezuela tanker detention.
newsitem.headline: Intertanko concerned at Venezuela tanker detention.

text.p: Intertanko, the International Association of Independent Tanker Owners, on Friday expressed impatience at the continued detention of the Nissos Amorgos and its captain in Venezuela after the vessel was grounded and spilt oil in the Maracaibo Channel in February.
"Intertanko is deeply concerned that limited progress has been made in the matter despite a number of positive initiatives intended to meet local demands.

"It is the expectation and hope of Intertanko that international conventions governing claims and liability to which Venezuela is a signatory will provide prompt disposition of this matter without continued detention of the vessel and crew," the Oslo-based organisation said in a statement.
Around 25,000 barrels of oil were reported spilt when the tanker was grounded on February 28.
So far this year there have been three serious tanker groundings in the Maracaibo Channel, through which 70 percent of Venezuela's oil exports pass.

Following these accidents, a 36 foot draught restriction has been introduced in the Channel, down from the normal 39.5 feet. Shipbrokers say this could cut Venezuela's oil exports by 150,000 barrels per day.
Venezuelan Transport Minister General Moises Orozco Graterol said earlier this month that the Nissos Amorgos may have hit the wreck of a ship that sank more than 10 years ago.
He also said he was study the idea of enlarging the Channel to meet the growing size of ships using it.
